VDR-CSO-DET.explanation: Weekly manual reviews cover servers and availability alerts, but disclosure intake and process-weakness detection are incomplete.
VDR-CSO-DET.customerRisk: Missed weaknesses could disrupt the public-information workspace or expose information agencies placed there.
VDR-CSO-DET.providerCompensation: A small inventory and daily uptime checks make operational changes easier to investigate.
VDR-CSO-DET.agencyCompensation: Agencies should retain source copies and avoid sensitive data or critical workloads.

VDR-CSO-RES.explanation: A weekly spreadsheet review tracks major findings, but ownership and exploitation checks are not complete for every vulnerability.
VDR-CSO-RES.customerRisk: Unassigned findings may remain open and cause preventable service interruptions.
VDR-CSO-RES.providerCompensation: An on-call operator isolates unstable components and keeps restoration instructions current.
VDR-CSO-RES.agencyCompensation: Agencies should keep an alternate publication channel and avoid critical workloads.

VDR-CSO-FAV.explanation: We have not yet recorded failures of our detection and response processes as vulnerabilities.
VDR-CSO-FAV.customerRisk: Repeated review failures may hide exposures that affect agency information or availability.
VDR-CSO-FAV.providerCompensation: The weekly operations meeting assigns corrective work in a separate issue list.
VDR-CSO-FAV.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request unresolved process issues before expanding their use.

VDR-CSO-DFR.explanation: Simple isolation and backups support resilience, but the small team has not redesigned shared components that complicate recovery.
VDR-CSO-DFR.customerRisk: A shared-component failure could interrupt multiple agency workspaces.
VDR-CSO-DFR.providerCompensation: We test restores monthly and restrict administrative access.
VDR-CSO-DFR.agencyCompensation: Agencies should maintain an alternate service and avoid time-critical dependencies.

VDR-CSO-ADT.explanation: Budget limits keep vulnerability detection and response largely manual, beyond basic uptime alerts.
VDR-CSO-ADT.completionTargetExplanation: We have not selected an affordable monitoring service.
VDR-CSO-ADT.customerRisk: Manual checks can miss emerging weaknesses between reviews.
VDR-CSO-ADT.providerCompensation: Operators inspect the small resource inventory weekly and investigate uptime alarms daily.
VDR-CSO-ADT.agencyCompensation: Agencies should report unusual behavior promptly and keep sensitive data elsewhere.

VDR-CSO-DAC.explanation: Changes receive manual checks because our deployment scripts do not trigger vulnerability detection.
VDR-CSO-DAC.customerRisk: A release could introduce a weakness that affects agency access or content.
VDR-CSO-DAC.providerCompensation: The operator reviews changed settings and tests rollback before release.
VDR-CSO-DAC.agencyCompensation: Agencies can defer new integrations until the release review is available.

VDR-CSO-MSP.explanation: Manual assessment uses restricted maintenance access without disabling protective controls or opening additional network paths.

VDR-CSO-AKE.explanation: Operators check major images against KEVs, but the release checklist does not yet cover every machine component.
VDR-CSO-AKE.customerRisk: An overlooked component could expose agency workspaces to known exploitation.
VDR-CSO-AKE.providerCompensation: We limit exposed services and remove unused components.
VDR-CSO-AKE.agencyCompensation: Agencies should avoid sensitive content and restrict unnecessary integrations.

VDR-CSO-SIR.explanation: We inspect every machine in the small environment and do not use the optional sampling permission.

VDR-TFR-NMV.explanation: Some procedures receive quarterly verification and validation, but staffing gaps leave others overdue.
VDR-TFR-NMV.customerRisk: Outdated instructions may delay recovery or lead to incorrect handling of agency information.
VDR-TFR-NMV.providerCompensation: Operators test restoration steps monthly and review known documentation gaps weekly.
VDR-TFR-NMV.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request current recovery instructions and keep independent copies of their content.

VDR-TFR-PDD.explanation: Servers receive weekly reviews, but some identity and process resources miss the Class B monthly drift-detection interval.
VDR-TFR-PDD.customerRisk: Unnoticed access or procedure changes may affect agency information.
VDR-TFR-PDD.providerCompensation: We restrict administrative access and review change tickets weekly.
VDR-TFR-PDD.agencyCompensation: Agencies should periodically review their accounts and report unexpected permissions.

VDR-TFR-PCD.explanation: Stable servers are reviewed quarterly, but some non-machine resources have not received complete detection checks within six months.
VDR-TFR-PCD.customerRisk: Hidden weaknesses in stable resources could undermine service recovery.
VDR-TFR-PCD.providerCompensation: Operators test the restoration path monthly and record discovered weaknesses.
VDR-TFR-PCD.agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask for the last review date for dependencies they rely on.

VDR-TFR-PVR.explanation: We prioritize availability exposures, but cannot yet demonstrate all Class B impact reductions within the applicable PAIN timeframes.
VDR-TFR-PVR.completionTargetExplanation: Supplier fixes and incomplete tracking prevent a reliable completion estimate.
VDR-TFR-PVR.customerRisk: Other exposures may persist beyond recommended intervals and affect agency content or access.
VDR-TFR-PVR.providerCompensation: We disable affected optional features and retain tested backups.
VDR-TFR-PVR.agencyCompensation: Agencies should avoid critical workloads and keep sensitive information outside this service.

VDR-TFR-RMN.explanation: Routine maintenance resolves outage-related findings, but other residual vulnerabilities lack consistent scheduling.
VDR-TFR-RMN.customerRisk: Deferred weaknesses may accumulate and affect agency information.
VDR-TFR-RMN.providerCompensation: Weekly reviews retain those findings and prioritize any change in likely impact.
VDR-TFR-RMN.agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask about unresolved findings before extending service use.

VDR-TFR-KEV.explanation: We patch exposed KEVs promptly, but do not yet consistently remediate fully mitigated KEVs by catalog due dates.
VDR-TFR-KEV.customerRisk: Failure of an interim mitigation could restore a known exploitation path.
VDR-TFR-KEV.providerCompensation: Operators recheck filtering and disable affected optional components.
VDR-TFR-KEV.agencyCompensation: Agencies should disconnect affected integrations until remediation is confirmed.

VDR-TFR-PSD.explanation: Operators perform vulnerability detection on every machine at least once every seven days, covering more than the Class B representative-sample minimum.

VDR-TFR-MVX.explanation: This is a Rev5 Class B offering, so the 20x-specific machine-verification rule does not apply; VDR-TFR-MVF is the relevant rule.

VDR-TFR-MVF.explanation: Weekly checks verify availability, but full validation of machine configurations against intended behavior remains incomplete.
VDR-TFR-MVF.customerRisk: Undetected configuration errors may affect agency access or information.
VDR-TFR-MVF.providerCompensation: Operators compare key service settings and test restores monthly.
VDR-TFR-MVF.agencyCompensation: Agencies should use this workspace only for noncritical public information.

VER-EVA-ELX.explanation: Weekly reviews evaluate major exploitation prerequisites, but supporting evidence is incomplete for some findings.
VER-EVA-ELX.customerRisk: We may underestimate vulnerabilities affecting agency workspaces.
VER-EVA-ELX.providerCompensation: The operator treats uncertain findings conservatively and disables exposed optional features.
VER-EVA-ELX.agencyCompensation: Agencies should keep sensitive data elsewhere and request review of concerning findings.

VER-EVA-EIR.explanation: Reviews cover direct internet exposure, but indirect payload paths through imports and logs are not fully assessed.
VER-EVA-EIR.customerRisk: A vulnerable internal component could process hostile input despite network isolation.
VER-EVA-EIR.providerCompensation: We restrict imports and filter external input at the service boundary.
VER-EVA-EIR.agencyCompensation: Agencies should avoid untrusted uploads and disable unused integrations.

VER-EVA-EPA.explanation: Weekly reviews assign provisional PAIN ratings emphasizing outages, but confidentiality, integrity, and multi-agency effects need fuller analysis.
VER-EVA-EPA.customerRisk: Incomplete impact estimates may understate the consequences for agency customers.
VER-EVA-EPA.providerCompensation: We restrict the service to public-information use and escalate uncertain ratings.
VER-EVA-EPA.agencyCompensation: Agencies should verify that their content is public and avoid mission-critical dependencies.

VER-EVA-AIA.explanation: Our manual checklist assumes exploitation can be automated unless we retain technical evidence proving otherwise.

VER-EVA-GRV.explanation: The small team tracks each finding separately and has not established contextual vulnerability groups.
VER-EVA-GRV.completionTargetExplanation: The small inventory currently makes individual tracking more practical.
VER-EVA-GRV.customerRisk: Related findings may receive inconsistent handling and consume review time.
VER-EVA-GRV.providerCompensation: A single operator checks the full register each week for shared causes.
VER-EVA-GRV.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request one explanation for related findings affecting their workspace.

VER-EVA-EFP.explanation: Operators verify obvious scanner errors, but lack time to investigate every potential false positive.
VER-EVA-EFP.customerRisk: Unconfirmed findings can divert effort from genuine agency risks.
VER-EVA-EFP.providerCompensation: Uncertain findings remain open and high-impact cases receive priority.
VER-EVA-EFP.agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask for the evidence behind any dismissed finding.

VER-EVA-EFA.explanation: Reviews consider availability, reachability, and basic exploitability, but do not consistently document all eight contextual factors.
VER-EVA-EFA.customerRisk: Incomplete context may hide privilege escalation or interacting vulnerabilities.
VER-EVA-EFA.providerCompensation: We limit privileges and review known incidents during the weekly assessment.
VER-EVA-EFA.agencyCompensation: Agencies should describe their use case and avoid sensitive or critical workloads.

VER-RPT-PER.explanation: Weekly updates cover major findings, but some verification and validation activity is missing from reports to necessary parties.
VER-RPT-PER.customerRisk: Agencies may lack a complete basis for continued-use decisions.
VER-RPT-PER.providerCompensation: We provide the underlying operations log on request through controlled sharing.
VER-RPT-PER.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request missing records and limit use until questions are resolved.

VER-RPT-VDT.explanation: Our spreadsheet includes identifiers and current ratings but lacks complete historical reductions, evaluation times, and next-reduction details.
VER-RPT-VDT.customerRisk: Agencies may not be able to judge whether risk is declining on time.
VER-RPT-VDT.providerCompensation: Operators retain dated work notes and review unresolved findings weekly.
VER-RPT-VDT.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request those notes and keep independent records of important exposures.

VER-RPT-AVI.explanation: Accepted findings include reasons and identifiers, but evaluation times and agency mitigation details are incomplete.
VER-RPT-AVI.customerRisk: Agencies may misunderstand the duration or consequences of accepted risk.
VER-RPT-AVI.providerCompensation: We list known limitations in the monthly report and offer a manual review.
VER-RPT-AVI.agencyCompensation: Agencies should seek clarification before accepting affected use cases.

VER-RPT-NID.explanation: The operator shares risk information with necessary parties through restricted channels and removes exploit-enabling technical detail from public notices.

VER-RPT-HLO.explanation: Monthly summaries cover maintenance and outages, but do not yet summarize every detection and response activity.
VER-RPT-HLO.customerRisk: Agencies may overestimate the breadth of our review program.
VER-RPT-HLO.providerCompensation: The full operations log remains available through controlled sharing.
VER-RPT-HLO.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request separate testing and disclosure records.

VER-RPT-RPD.explanation: We do not currently exercise optional public vulnerability disclosure and continue required controlled reporting to necessary parties.

VER-TFR-MHR.explanation: All necessary parties receive the same human-readable monthly report, with implementation gaps and service limitations identified.

VER-TFR-MAV.explanation: The weekly register flags elapsed 192-day cases, but we do not yet consistently mark findings accepted when missing that limit is foreseeable.
VER-TFR-MAV.customerRisk: Agencies may mistake a long-term exposure for work that will finish within the limit.
VER-TFR-MAV.providerCompensation: The monthly report lists supplier delays and known unresolved limitations.
VER-TFR-MAV.agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask whether any planned fix lacks a credible completion date.

VER-TFR-MRH.explanation: The spreadsheet has no automated JSON retrieval interface, and a small team has not funded one.
VER-TFR-MRH.completionTargetExplanation: Funding and implementation timing remain undecided.
VER-TFR-MRH.customerRisk: Agency tools cannot automatically monitor historical activity.
VER-TFR-MRH.providerCompensation: We provide manually assembled history through controlled sharing on request.
VER-TFR-MRH.agencyCompensation: Agencies can reconcile the history with monthly reports and retain their own copies.

VER-TFR-EVU.explanation: Every detected finding receives a weekly initial review, but complete evaluation under VER-EVA is not consistently finished within seven days.
VER-TFR-EVU.customerRisk: Incomplete evaluations may delay agency decisions about exposures between reviews.
VER-TFR-EVU.providerCompensation: The operator escalates suspected high-impact findings immediately and tracks unfinished assessments.
VER-TFR-EVU.agencyCompensation: Agencies should request completed assessments before expanding use beyond noncritical public information.

VER-TFR-IRI.explanation: We exercise the Class B option to treat internet-reachable likely exploitable findings above N3 as reportable incidents until reduced to N3 or below.

VER-TFR-NRI.explanation: We also exercise the Class B option to treat non-internet-reachable likely exploitable N5 findings as reportable incidents until reduced to N4 or below.
